# caveowl

> A recipe for teaching ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B (a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B fine-tune) to answer in
> terse "caveman" style through a bf16 LoRA trained with Unsloth, while keeping its tool calls,
> code and agent-skill use at the stock model's level. This file tells a coding agent how to run
> the whole pipeline on its user's machine: what to ask the user first, every command in order,
> how to check each step, and what usually goes wrong.

- [README](README.md): what caveowl does, results, the data slices and the gate, for people
- [config.toml](config.toml): the recipe (data shares, LoRA targets, hyperparameters)
- [docs/runs.md](docs/runs.md): five real runs, each failure and its fix, with numbers
- [docs/internals.md](docs/internals.md): rendering, loss masks, LoRA targets, memory

## Instructions for agents

You are implementing this pipeline for your user. It takes a day or more of machine time, needs
most of a large GPU, and can spend money on the Anthropic API. Work in this order, check each
step's output before the next, and stop and ask whenever a check fails or a decision below is
not yet made.

### Ask the user before starting

1. **Hardware.** bf16 training peaks at ~88 GiB of GPU memory (measured). Confirm the GPU and its
   memory (`rocm-smi --showmeminfo vram` / `--showmeminfo gtt`, or `nvidia-smi`). On unified-memory
   machines (AMD Strix Halo, Apple-class designs) the limit is the GPU-visible pool (GTT), not
   system RAM. Below ~90 GB, the only route is `load_in_4bit = true` in config.toml, which is
   untested and which Unsloth advises against for this architecture: say so and let the user
   decide.
2. **Other model servers.** Anything else holding GPU memory must stop during training, merging
   and GGUF conversion. Ask which services those are and how the user wants them stopped and
   restored. List every port that serves something the user relies on in
   `~/.config/caveowl/live-ports` (space-separated, e.g. `8080 8081`); every builder and gate in
   this repo refuses those ports.
3. **Bench port.** A free port for serving the stock model and the candidate (default 8110; the
   skill builder also uses that port + 1 for a logging proxy). Set `BENCH_PORT` and
   `CAVEOWL_BENCH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:$BENCH_PORT/v1`.
4. **Will the model run as an agent?** The skill-trajectory slice and the skill gates need the
   `pi` coding agent (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) with the user's skills installed in
   `~/.pi/agent/skills/`. The bundled prompt sets target the author's skills (weather, system
   health, PDF reading, summarizing, humanizing text, explaining simply, a coffee tracker). If the
   user's skills differ, either write prompt sets for theirs (copy the pattern in
   `data/skill_run2.py`, keeping fixtures and prompts disjoint from `eval/skill_gate_wide.py`) or
   set `skill_share = 0`. Without pi, also skip the pi-based gates.
5. **API spend.** The caveman text pairs, the tool slice's prose and the agent-loop answers are
   rewritten by Claude through the Message Batches API. Every rewrite script has `--dry-run`,
   which prints the row count and a cost estimate and sends nothing. Show the user that estimate
   and get an explicit yes before running anything with `--confirm-spend`. Never pass
   `--confirm-spend` on your own judgement. The key comes from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the
   environment; never write it to a file or a log.
6. **Serving temperature.** The released adapter is served at 0.3. Gate at the temperature the
   user will serve at; at 0.6 the adapter dropped a requested tool argument in 2 of 90 samples.

### Rules while working

- Run long jobs detached (`systemd-run --user`, `tmux`, or `nohup`) and poll their logs; training
  takes ~14 hours on a Strix Halo and resumes from its newest checkpoint if interrupted.
- Never run `uv run` or `pip install` inside another project's directory or venv; `uv run` syncs
  that project's environment.
- Keep scratch work out of RAM-backed `/tmp` when it is large (checkpoints, GGUFs: tens of GB).
- Do not point any builder or gate at a live server. If you are unsure whether a port is live,
  ask.
- Report results with their numbers, including failures. A gate result that is worse than stock
  is a finding for the user, not something to hide or rerun until it passes.

### 1. Environment

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 ~/venvs/caveowl
# torch first, for the platform: ROCm wheel on AMD, CUDA wheel on NVIDIA. Verify:
~/venvs/caveowl/bin/python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available())"
uv pip install --python ~/venvs/caveowl/bin/python "unsloth[amd]"      # "unsloth" on NVIDIA
uv pip install --python ~/venvs/caveowl/bin/python flash-linear-attention==0.5.2 anthropic tiktoken
export PY=~/venvs/caveowl/bin/python HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1
```

Check: `torch.cuda.is_available()` prints True (ROCm builds report through the same API). Known
good: unsloth 2026.10.3, transformers 5.17.0, torch 2.11.0+rocm7.13.0. On ROCm a warning that
`causal_conv1d` falls back to PyTorch is expected.

Also needed: a llama.cpp build with `llama-server`, `llama-imatrix`, `llama-quantize`,
`llama-perplexity` and its `convert_hf_to_gguf.py`; `bwrap` (bubblewrap) for the sandboxed code
tests; ~250 GB of free disk.

### 2. Models

```bash
hf download ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B --revision 10fbf86fed7ecee4a061f8b499a618f46001cac1 \
    --local-dir ~/models/ornith-35b-hf
hf download ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-GGUF --include "*Q4_K_M*" "*mmproj*" --local-dir ~/models/ornith-35b
```

Check: 16 `*.safetensors` shards plus `model.safetensors.index.json` in `~/models/ornith-35b-hf`.
config.toml's `[model] base` must point there.

### 3. Model-independent data (Claude rewrites; ask before spending)

Caveman text pairs. Build them with https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/cavegemma's corpus pipeline
(`data/build_prompts.py`/`build_corpus.py` there), then rewrite and split:

```bash
# in a cavegemma checkout: build the source rows (its build_prompts.py / build_corpus.py), then copy
# its data/out/corpus_raw.jsonl here as data/out/corpus_raw.jsonl
$PY data/synthesize_batch.py --in data/out/corpus_raw.jsonl --dry-run          # show the estimate
$PY data/synthesize_batch.py --in data/out/corpus_raw.jsonl --confirm-spend    # after a yes
# -> data/out/raw_pairs.jsonl. Filter and split with cavegemma's data/filter.py and data/split.py,
# then save the splits as data/in/text_train.jsonl and data/in/text_eval.jsonl
# (rows {"prompt", "target", ...}; the release had 1,689 train / 187 eval).
```

Tool-call slice:

```bash
$PY data/build_tool_corpus.py                                   # -> data/out/tool_corpus.jsonl
$PY data/synthesize_batch.py --tool-corpus data/out/tool_corpus.jsonl --fewshot 4 --dry-run
$PY data/synthesize_batch.py --tool-corpus data/out/tool_corpus.jsonl --fewshot 4 --confirm-spend
$PY data/filter_tool_pairs.py                                    # -> data/in/tool.jsonl
```

Check: `data/in/text_train.jsonl` (~1,700 rows), `data/in/text_eval.jsonl` (~190) and
`data/in/tool.jsonl` (the release kept 481 of 600) exist; the filter reports its rejection
reasons. Without tiktoken installed, token counts fall back to the model's tokenizer.

### 4. Serve the stock model on the bench port

```bash
BENCH_PORT=8110 LLAMA_SERVER=<path>/llama-server \
    MMPROJ=~/models/ornith-35b/mmproj-Ornith-1.5-35B-BF16.gguf \
    nohup scripts/serve_bench.sh ~/models/ornith-35b/Ornith-1.5-35B-Q4_K_M.gguf 0.6 > bench.log 2>&1 &
until curl -sf localhost:8110/health; do sleep 5; done
```

The flags in `scripts/serve_bench.sh` should match how the user will serve the model; adjust them
there, once, so stock and candidate are always served identically.

### 5. Self-distilled data from the stock model

```bash
$PY data/build_anchor.py                                   # MBPP Python, test-filtered
$PY data/build_anchor_ultra.py --validate                  # UltraData-Code sh/R/Rust, reference tests in bwrap
$PY data/build_anchor_ultra.py
$PY data/merge_anchors.py                                  # also holds out 90 tasks for the gate
$PY data/build_bound_anchor.py --n 900                     # tool calls that keep a stated bound
$PY data/build_think_anchor.py --n 450                     # thinking-on rows
$PY data/build_skill_anchor.py --extra-attempts 2 --max-len 16384   # only with pi (see question 4)
```

Agent loops (optional, needs the Claude rewrite; otherwise set `ext_share = 0`):

```bash
hf download julien-c/synthtraces --repo-type dataset --local-dir data/out/ext/synthtraces
$PY data/build_synthtraces.py                              # -> data/out/ext_traj.jsonl
$PY data/synthesize_batch.py --tool-corpus data/out/ext_traj.jsonl --tool-out data/out/ext_traj_cave.jsonl \
    --model claude-haiku-5-5 --dry-run
$PY data/synthesize_batch.py --tool-corpus data/out/ext_traj.jsonl --tool-out data/out/ext_traj_cave.jsonl \
    --model claude-haiku-5-5 --confirm-spend
$PY data/skills_wrap_ext.py                                # -> data/out/ext_traj_cave_skills.jsonl
# skills_wrap_ext.py copies skill markup from your skill trajectories, so build those first.
```

Point `skill_path` in config.toml at the skill file(s) you built. Then stop the bench server and
check the mix without loading weights:

```bash
$PY train_unsloth.py --config config.toml --prepare-only
```

Check: no slice reports `missing`; per-slice rows are in the README's ballpark; the masked samples
show loss (`⟦ ⟧`) only on assistant content, tool calls and `<|im_end|>`, plus the reasoning in
thinking-on rows. A slice with many `prefix_mismatch` or `marker_in_content` drops means the data
does not match the template.

### 6. Train

Stop the other GPU users first (question 2). Then:

```bash
$PY train_unsloth.py --config config_smoke.toml --no-resume 2>&1 | tee artifacts/smoke.log
$PY train_unsloth.py --config config.toml 2>&1 | tee artifacts/train.log       # detached
```

Check the smoke log before the full run: trainable parameters ~0.94B with a non-zero
"routed-expert LoRA" figure (0.0M means Unsloth's MoE path did not attach: stop and report), peak
memory below the GPU's limit with a few GiB to spare, and seconds per step (multiply by the
optimiser steps `--prepare-only` printed for the run time). During the full run, losses are in
`artifacts/adapter/checkpoint-*/trainer_state.json`; expect ~1.1 at the start falling to ~0.6-0.8.

### 7. Merge and convert

```bash
LLAMA=<llama.cpp checkout> bash merge_and_gguf.sh 2>&1 | tee artifacts/merge.log
```

Check: the log ends with the Q4_K_M path and the merge's tensor checks passed (untouched tensors,
vision tower and MTP head byte-identical to the base). Restore the user's servers afterwards.

### 8. Gate

```bash
T=0.3 OWL=artifacts/gguf/Ornith-1.5-35B-caveowl-Q4_K_M.gguf OWL_LABEL=caveowl \
    KIT=<llm-bench-kit checkout> PI_MODELS_JSON=<pi models.json with a "local-cand" provider at the bench port> \
    PERPLEXITY=<llama-perplexity> WIKI=<wikitext-2 wiki.test.raw> bash scripts/gate.sh
```

`KIT` is https://github.com/sjvrensburg/llm-bench-kit. Add `AGENTS_MD=<the user's AGENTS.md>` to
run the skill gate a second time under the user's own agent instructions. The pass rule for
every check is "candidate at least as good as stock, served the same way, run the same evening";
the README's "The gate" lists what each check catches. Results are in `eval/out/gate/`.

When a check fails, read the failing sessions in `eval/out/` before concluding anything, rerun
that one check with more samples (stock varies between runs), and report both numbers. The fixes
that worked for each failure seen so far are in docs/runs.md:

| Symptom | Cause found | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| a skill family below stock, `skill_not_read` | no trajectories for that family | add self-distilled trajectories for it |
| PDF or other simple tasks solved with bash, skill never opened | data rows with no skills listed in the system prompt | list (inapplicable) skills in every agent row |
| empty answers when thinking is on | training rows were all thinking-off | thinking-on rows (`data/build_think_anchor.py`) |
| a stated tool argument dropped at the served temperature | style pressure on optional arguments | bounded tool-call rows, more weight; serve at 0.3 |
| process killed while loading the checkpoint | mmap kept a CPU copy of the weights | already fixed: `owl_load.py` loads with pread |

### 9. Serve

Serve the Q4_K_M with the stock model's vision projector, `--jinja`, `--reasoning-format
deepseek`, the gated temperature, top-k 20, top-p 0.95. Anything that names the model (client
configs, model ids) must be updated together; ask the user which clients use it.
